{"content": "     1|#!/usr/bin/env python3
     2|"""
     3|SQLite State Store for Hermes Agent.
     4|
     5|Provides persistent session storage with FTS5 full-text search, replacing
     6|the per-session JSONL file approach. Stores session metadata, full message
     7|history, and model configuration for CLI and gateway sessions.
     8|
     9|Key design decisions:
    10|- WAL mode for concurrent readers + one writer (gateway multi-platform)
    11|- FTS5 virtual table for fast text search across all session messages
    12|- Compression-triggered session splitting via parent_session_id chains
    13|- Batch runner and RL trajectories are NOT stored here (separate systems)
    14|- Session source tagging ('cli', 'telegram', 'discord', etc.) for filtering
    15|"""
    16|
    17|import json
    18|import logging
    19|import random
    20|import re
    21|import sqlite3
    22|import threading
    23|import time
    24|from pathlib import Path
    25|from hermes_constants import get_hermes_home
    26|from typing import Any, Callable, Dict, List, Optional, TypeVar
    27|
    28|logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    29|
    30|T = TypeVar("T")
    31|
    32|DEFAULT_DB_PATH = get_hermes_home() / "state.db"
    33|
    34|SCHEMA_VERSION = 6
    35|
    36|SCHEMA_SQL = """
    37|CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS schema_version (
    38|    version INTEGER NOT NULL
    39|);
    40|
    41|CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sessions (
    42|    id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    43|    source TEXT NOT NULL,
    44|    user_id TEXT,
    45|    model TEXT,
    46|    model_config TEXT,
    47|    system_prompt TEXT,
    48|    parent_session_id TEXT,
    49|    started_at REAL NOT NULL,
    50|    ended_at REAL,
    51|    end_reason TEXT,
    52|    message_count INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    53|    tool_call_count INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    54|    input_tokens INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    55|    output_tokens INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    56|    cache_read_tokens INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    57|    cache_write_tokens INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    58|    reasoning_tokens INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    59|    billing_provider TEXT,
    60|    billing_base_url TEXT,
    61|    billing_mode TEXT,
    62|    estimated_cost_usd REAL,
    63|    actual_cost_usd REAL,
    64|    cost_status TEXT,
    65|    cost_source TEXT,
    66|    pricing_version TEXT,
    67|    title TEXT,
    68|    FOREIGN KEY (parent_session_id) REFERENCES sessions(id)
    69|);
    70|
    71|CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS messages (
    72|    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    73|    session_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES sessions(id),
    74|    role TEXT NOT NULL,
    75|    content TEXT,
    76|    tool_call_id TEXT,
    77|    tool_calls TEXT,
    78|    tool_name TEXT,
    79|    timestamp REAL NOT NULL,
    80|    token_count INTEGER,
    81|    finish_reason TEXT,
    82|    reasoning TEXT,
    83|    reasoning_details TEXT,
    84|    codex_reasoning_items TEXT
    85|);
    86|
    87|CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_sessions_source ON sessions(source);
    88|CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_sessions_parent ON sessions(parent_session_id);
    89|CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_sessions_started ON sessions(started_at DESC);
    90|CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_messages_session ON messages(session_id, timestamp);
    91|"""
    92|
    93|FTS_SQL = """
    94|CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE IF NOT EXISTS messages_fts USING fts5(
    95|    content,
    96|    content=messages,
    97|    content_rowid=id
    98|);
    99|
   100|CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS messages_fts_insert AFTER INSERT ON messages BEGIN
   101|    INSERT INTO messages_fts(rowid, content) VALUES (new.id, new.content);
   102|END;
   103|
   104|CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS messages_fts_delete AFTER DELETE ON messages BEGIN
   105|    INSERT INTO messages_fts(messages_fts, rowid, content) VALUES('delete', old.id, old.content);
   106|END;
   107|
   108|CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS messages_fts_update AFTER UPDATE ON messages BEGIN
   109|    INSERT INTO messages_fts(messages_fts, rowid, content) VALUES('delete', old.id, old.content);
   110|    INSERT INTO messages_fts(rowid, content) VALUES (new.id, new.content);
   111|END;
   112|"""
   113|
   114|
   115|class SessionDB:
   116|    """
   117|    SQLite-backed session storage with FTS5 search.
   118|
   119|    Thread-safe for the common gateway pattern (multiple reader threads,
   120|    single writer via WAL mode). Each method opens its own cursor.
   121|    """
   122|
   123|    # ── Write-contention tuning ──
   124|    # With multiple hermes processes (gateway + CLI sessions + worktree agents)
   125|    # all sharing one state.db, WAL write-lock contention causes visible TUI
   126|    # freezes.  SQLite's built-in busy handler uses a deterministic sleep
   127|    # schedule that causes convoy effects under high concurrency.
   128|    #
   129|    # Instead, we keep the SQLite timeout short (1s) and handle retries at the
   130|    # application level with random jitter, which naturally staggers competing
   131|    # writers and avoids the convoy.
   132|    _WRITE_MAX_RETRIES = 15
   133|    _WRITE_RETRY_MIN_S = 0.020   # 20ms
   134|    _WRITE_RETRY_MAX_S = 0.150   # 150ms
   135|    # Attempt a PASSIVE WAL checkpoint every N successful writes.
   136|    _CHECKPOINT_EVERY_N_WRITES = 50
   137|
   138|    def __init__(self, db_path: Path = None):
   139|        self.db_path = db_path or DEFAULT_DB_PATH
   140|        self.db_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   141|
   142|        self._lock = threading.Lock()
   143|        self._write_count = 0
   144|        self._conn = sqlite3.connect(
   145|            str(self.db_path),
   146|            check_same_thread=False,
   147|            # Short timeout — application-level retry with random jitter
   148|            # handles contention instead of sitting in SQLite's internal
   149|            # busy handler for up to 30s.
   150|            timeout=1.0,
   151|            # Autocommit mode: Python's default isolation_level="" auto-starts
   152|            # transactions on DML, which conflicts with our explicit
   153|            # BEGIN IMMEDIATE.  None = we manage transactions ourselves.
   154|            isolation_level=None,
   155|        )
   156|        self._conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
   157|        self._conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL")
   158|        self._conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON")
   159|
   160|        self._init_schema()
   161|
   162|    # ── Core write helper ──
   163|
   164|    def _execute_write(self, fn: Callable[[sqlite3.Connection], T]) -> T:
   165|        """Execute a write transaction with BEGIN IMMEDIATE and jitter retry.
   166|
   167|        *fn* receives the connection and should perform INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE
   168|        statements.  The caller must NOT call ``commit()`` — that's handled
   169|        here after *fn* returns.
   170|
   171|        BEGIN IMMEDIATE acquires the WAL write lock at transaction start
   172|        (not at commit time), so lock contention surfaces immediately.
   173|        On ``database is locked``, we release the Python lock, sleep a
   174|        random 20-150ms, and retry — breaking the convoy pattern that
   175|        SQLite's built-in deterministic backoff creates.
   176|
   177|        Returns whatever *fn* returns.
   178|        """
   179|        last_err: Optional[Exception] = None
   180|        for attempt in range(self._WRITE_MAX_RETRIES):
   181|            try:
   182|                with self._lock:
   183|                    self._conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
   184|                    try:
   185|                        result = fn(self._conn)
   186|                        self._conn.commit()
   187|                    except BaseException:
   188|                        try:
   189|                            self._conn.rollback()
   190|                        except Exception:
   191|                            pass
   192|                        raise
   193|                # Success — periodic best-effort checkpoint.
   194|                self._write_count += 1
   195|                if self._write_count % self._CHECKPOINT_EVERY_N_WRITES == 0:
   196|                    self._try_wal_checkpoint()
   197|                return result
   198|            except sqlite3.OperationalError as exc:
   199|                err_msg = str(exc).lower()
   200|                if "locked" in err_msg or "busy" in err_msg:
   201|                    last_err = exc
   202|                    if attempt < self._WRITE_MAX_RETRIES - 1:
   203|                        jitter = random.uniform(
   204|                            self._WRITE_RETRY_MIN_S,
   205|                            self._WRITE_RETRY_MAX_S,
   206|                        )
   207|                        time.sleep(jitter)
   208|                        continue
   209|                # Non-lock error or retries exhausted — propagate.
   210|                raise
   211|        # Retries exhausted (shouldn't normally reach here).
   212|        raise last_err or sqlite3.OperationalError(
   213|            "database is locked after max retries"
   214|        )
   215|
   216|    def _try_wal_checkpoint(self) -> None:
   217|        """Best-effort PASSIVE WAL checkpoint.  Never blocks, never raises.
   218|
   219|        Flushes committed WAL frames back into the main DB file for any
   220|        frames that no other connection currently needs.  Keeps the WAL
   221|        from growing unbounded when many processes hold persistent
   222|        connections.
   223|        """
   224|        try:
   225|            with self._lock:
   226|                result = self._conn.execute(
   227|                    "PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(PASSIVE)"
   228|                ).fetchone()
   229|                if result and result[1] > 0:
   230|                    logger.debug(
   231|                        "WAL checkpoint: %d/%d pages checkpointed",
   232|                        result[2], result[1],
   233|                    )
   234|        except Exception:
   235|            pass  # Best effort — never fatal.
   236|
   237|    def close(self):
   238|        """Close the database connection.
   239|
   240|        Attempts a PASSIVE WAL checkpoint first so that exiting processes
   241|        help keep the WAL file from growing unbounded.
   242|        """
   243|        with self._lock:
   244|            if self._conn:
   245|                try:
   246|                    self._conn.execute("PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(PASSIVE)")
   247|                except Exception:
   248|                    pass
   249|                self._conn.close()
   250|                self._conn = None
   251|
   252|    def _init_schema(self):
   253|        """Create tables and FTS if they don't exist, run migrations."""
   254|        cursor = self._conn.cursor()
   255|
   256|        cursor.executescript(SCHEMA_SQL)
   257|
   258|        # Check schema version and run migrations
   259|        cursor.execute("SELECT version FROM schema_version LIMIT 1")
   260|        row = cursor.fetchone()
   261|        if row is None:
   262|            cursor.execute("INSERT INTO schema_version (version) VALUES (?)", (SCHEMA_VERSION,))
   263|        else:
   264|            current_version = row["version"] if isinstance(row, sqlite3.Row) else row[0]
   265|            if current_version < 2:
   266|                # v2: add finish_reason column to messages
   267|                try:
   268|                    cursor.execute("ALTER TABLE messages ADD COLUMN finish_reason TEXT")
   269|                except sqlite3.OperationalError:
   270|                    pass  # Column already exists
   271|                cursor.execute("UPDATE schema_version SET version = 2")
   272|            if current_version < 3:
   273|                # v3: add title column to sessions
   274|                try:
   275|                    cursor.execute("ALTER TABLE sessions ADD COLUMN title TEXT")
   276|                except sqlite3.OperationalError:
   277|                    pass  # Column already exists
   278|                cursor.execute("UPDATE schema_version SET version = 3")
   279|            if current_version < 4:
   280|                # v4: add unique index on title (NULLs allowed, only non-NULL must be unique)
   281|                try:
   282|                    cursor.execute(
   283|                        "CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_sessions_title_unique "
   284|                        "ON sessions(title) WHERE title IS NOT NULL"
   285|                    )
   286|                except sqlite3.OperationalError:
   287|                    pass  # Index already exists
   288|                cursor.execute("UPDATE schema_version SET version = 4")
   289|            if current_version < 5:
   290|                new_columns = [
   291|                    ("cache_read_tokens", "INTEGER DEFAULT 0"),
   292|                    ("cache_write_tokens", "INTEGER DEFAULT 0"),
   293|                    ("reasoning_tokens", "INTEGER DEFAULT 0"),
   294|                    ("billing_provider", "TEXT"),
   295|                    ("billing_base_url", "TEXT"),
   296|                    ("billing_mode", "TEXT"),
   297|                    ("estimated_cost_usd", "REAL"),
   298|                    ("actual_cost_usd", "REAL"),
   299|                    ("cost_status", "TEXT"),
   300|                    ("cost_source", "TEXT"),
   301|                    ("pricing_version", "TEXT"),
   302|                ]
   303|                for name, column_type in new_columns:
   304|                    try:
   305|                        # name and column_type come from the hardcoded tuple above,
   306|                        # not user input. Double-quote identifier escaping is applied
   307|                        # as defense-in-depth; SQLite DDL cannot be parameterized.
   308|                        safe_name = name.replace('"', '""')
   309|                        cursor.execute(f'ALTER TABLE sessions ADD COLUMN "{safe_name}" {column_type}')
   310|                    except sqlite3.OperationalError:
   311|                        pass
   312|                cursor.execute("UPDATE schema_version SET version = 5")
   313|            if current_version < 6:
   314|                # v6: add reasoning columns to messages table — preserves assistant
   315|                # reasoning text and structured reasoning_details across gateway
   316|                # session turns.  Without these, reasoning chains are lost on
   317|                # session reload, breaking multi-turn reasoning continuity for
   318|                # providers that replay reasoning (OpenRouter, OpenAI, Nous).
   319|                for col_name, col_type in [
   320|                    ("reasoning", "TEXT"),
   321|                    ("reasoning_details", "TEXT"),
   322|                    ("codex_reasoning_items", "TEXT"),
   323|                ]:
   324|                    try:
   325|                        safe = col_name.replace('"', '""')
   326|                        cursor.execute(
   327|                            f'ALTER TABLE messages ADD COLUMN "{safe}" {col_type}'
   328|                        )
   329|                    except sqlite3.OperationalError:
   330|                        pass  # Column already exists
   331|                cursor.execute("UPDATE schema_version SET version = 6")
   332|
   333|        # Unique title index — always ensure it exists (safe to run after migrations
   334|        # since the title column is guaranteed to exist at this point)
   335|        try:
   336|            cursor.execute(
   337|                "CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_sessions_title_unique "
   338|                "ON sessions(title) WHERE title IS NOT NULL"
   339|            )
   340|        except sqlite3.OperationalError:
   341|            pass  # Index already exists
   342|
   343|        # FTS5 setup (separate because CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE can't be in executescript with IF NOT EXISTS reliably)
   344|        try:
   345|            cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM messages_fts LIMIT 0")
   346|        except sqlite3.OperationalError:
   347|            cursor.executescript(FTS_SQL)
   348|
   349|        self._conn.commit()

   351|    # =========================================================================
   352|    # Session lifecycle
   353|    # =========================================================================
   354|
   355|    def create_session(
   356|        self,
   357|        session_id: str,
   358|        source: str,
   359|        model: str = None,
   360|        model_config: Dict[str, Any] = None,
   361|        system_prompt: str = None,
   362|        user_id: str = None,
   363|        parent_session_id: str = None,
   364|    ) -> str:
   365|        """Create a new session record. Returns the session_id."""
   366|        def _do(conn):
   367|            conn.execute(
   368|                """INSERT OR IGNORE INTO sessions (id, source, user_id, model, model_config,
   369|                   system_prompt, parent_session_id, started_at)
   370|                   VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)""",
   371|                (
   372|                    session_id,
   373|                    source,
   374|                    user_id,
   375|                    model,
   376|                    json.dumps(model_config) if model_config else None,
   377|                    system_prompt,
   378|                    parent_session_id,
   379|                    time.time(),
   380|                ),
   381|            )
   382|        self._execute_write(_do)
   383|        return session_id
   384|
   385|    def end_session(self, session_id: str, end_reason: str) -> None:
   386|        """Mark a session as ended."""
   387|        def _do(conn):
   388|            conn.execute(
   389|                "UPDATE sessions SET ended_at = ?, end_reason = ? WHERE id = ?",
   390|                (time.time(), end_reason, session_id),
   391|            )
   392|        self._execute_write(_do)
   393|
   394|    def reopen_session(self, session_id: str) -> None:
   395|        """Clear ended_at/end_reason so a session can be resumed."""
   396|        def _do(conn):
   397|            conn.execute(
   398|                "UPDATE sessions SET ended_at = NULL, end_reason = NULL WHERE id = ?",
   399|                (session_id,),
   400|            )
   401|        self._execute_write(_do)
   402|
   403|    def update_system_prompt(self, session_id: str, system_prompt: str) -> None:
   404|        """Store the full assembled system prompt snapshot."""
   405|        def _do(conn):
   406|            conn.execute(
   407|                "UPDATE sessions SET system_prompt = ? WHERE id = ?",
   408|                (system_prompt, session_id),
   409|            )
   410|        self._execute_write(_do)

   412|    def update_token_counts(
   413|        self,
   414|        session_id: str,
   415|        input_tokens: int = 0,
   416|        output_tokens: int = 0,
   417|        model: str = None,
   418|        cache_read_tokens: int = 0,
   419|        cache_write_tokens: int = 0,
   420|        reasoning_tokens: int = 0,
   421|        estimated_cost_usd: Optional[float] = None,
   422|        actual_cost_usd: Optional[float] = None,
   423|        cost_status: Optional[str] = None,
   424|        cost_source: Optional[str] = None,
   425|        pricing_version: Optional[str] = None,
   426|        billing_provider: Optional[str] = None,
   427|        billing_base_url: Optional[str] = None,
   428|        billing_mode: Optional[str] = None,
   429|        absolute: bool = False,
   430|    ) -> None:

   432|
   433|        When *absolute* is False (default), values are **incremented** — use
   434|        this for per-API-call deltas (CLI path).
   435|
   436|        When *absolute* is True, values are **set directly** — use this when
   437|        the caller already holds cumulative totals (gateway path, where the
   438|        cached agent accumulates across messages).
   439|        """

   442|                   input_tokens = ?,
